TriCalculator.cos:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the cosine of x by calling taylor(x, 50) and rounding the resulting value to 10 decimal places." cos]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The current object providing the taylor method and any internal state used by the Taylor approximation."
        <REF> x </REF>: numeric "The input value for which the cosine is approximated."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: float "The Taylor-series cosine approximation rounded to 10 decimal places."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.taylor(x, 50) to compute the Taylor-series approximation of cosine at x using 50 terms. RESULT taylor_result]
            [COMMAND Round taylor_result to 10 decimal places with round(). RESULT rounded_result]
            [COMMAND Return rounded_result as the result of the cos method. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.factorial:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the factorial of a positive integer a by accumulating the product in b while decrementing a until a equals 1, then returns b; a value of 1 immediately returns 1." factorial]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> a </REF>: number "The value whose factorial is computed. For positive integers greater than 1, the loop terminates and returns a!. The value 1 skips the loop and returns 1. Values less than or equal to 0, as well as non-integral values that never become exactly 1, cause the loop to run indefinitely."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> b </REF>: number "The accumulated product of all integers from a down to 2 for positive integer a; equal to a! when a > 0. The method does not return for non-terminating edge cases."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize b to the constant integer 1. RESULT b]
            [COMMAND While a is not equal to 1, multiply b by the current value of a, then decrement a by 1. If the initial a is 1, the loop body is skipped; if a is less than or equal to 0 or a non-integral value that never becomes exactly 1, this loop does not terminate. RESULT b_and_a]
            [COMMAND Return the value of b as the computed factorial. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.taylor:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts the input angle x from degrees to radians and computes an alternating series of even powers divided by corresponding factorials, starting from 1 and iterating k from 1 to n-1, with odd-count iterations subtracting and even-count iterations adding." taylor]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: numeric "Input angle in degrees used in the series evaluation."
        <REF> n </REF>: integer "Loop upper bound; the series iterates over k from 1 to n-1 inclusive."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: numeric "The accumulated alternating-series value."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize accumulator a to 1. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Convert x from degrees to radians by computing x = (x / 180) * pi. RESULT x]
            [COMMAND Initialize count to 1 to control alternating signs. RESULT count]
            [COMMAND Iterate k over range(1, n), so k takes values 1 through n-1; if n <= 1, skip the loop body entirely. RESULT k]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over k, if count is odd, subtract (x ** (2 * k)) / self.factorial(2 * k) from a; otherwise, add (x ** (2 * k)) / self.factorial(2 * k) to a. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over k, after updating a, increment count by 1. RESULT count]
            [COMMAND Return the accumulated value a. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.sin:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the sine of an angle in degrees using a Taylor series expansion, stopping when the absolute value of the current term is below 1e-15, and returns the result rounded to 10 decimal places." sin]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: number "Input angle in degrees."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: number "Sine of x computed to 10 decimal places."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Convert the input angle x from degrees to radians by computing x = x / 180 * pi and replacing x with the radian value. RESULT x]
            [COMMAND Initialize accumulator g to 0. RESULT g]
            [COMMAND Initialize Taylor term t to the current radian value of x. RESULT t]
            [COMMAND Initialize term counter n to 1. RESULT n]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the pre-test loop condition fabs(t) >= 1e-15; while it is true, execute the following loop-body steps and then re-evaluate the condition. RESULT loop_condition]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, add the current term t to the accumulator g. RESULT g]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, increment the term counter n by 1. RESULT n]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, with n already incremented, compute the next term t as -t * x * x / (2 * n - 1) / (2 * n - 2). RESULT t]
            [COMMAND After the while loop exits, return round(g, 10) as the computed sine value. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.tan:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns the tangent of x as sin(x)/cos(x) rounded to 10 decimal places when cos(x) is nonzero, and returns False when cos(x) is zero." tan]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: numeric "Angle in radians for which to compute the tangent."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: float or bool "Rounded tangent value when cos(x) is nonzero; False when cos(x) is zero."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate self.cos(x) and assign the value to cos_x. RESULT cos_x]
            [COMMAND Check if cos_x is not equal to 0. RESULT condition_met]
            [COMMAND If condition_met is true, compute result = self.sin(x) / self.cos(x), calling self.cos(x) again as in the original code. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return round(result, 10). RESULT rounded_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: cos_x == 0]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return False. RESULT false_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
